name: gods-eye-view
description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
one_liner: A living 3D globe that shows real planes, ships, satellites, and earthquakes moving in real time, all from public data feeds.
buyer: TV newsrooms and documentary producers who need a dramatic, accurate live map on screen the moment a story breaks, without licensing an expensive intelligence platform.
business_use_cases: A news channel drops a live shot of the exact air traffic over an airport during a shutdown, generated on air in seconds.
A logistics blogger shows subscribers the real cargo ships stuck outside a port to explain a supply-chain delay.
A museum or science centre runs it on a big wall screen as an always-on 'watch the planet breathe' exhibit.

money_ideas.idea: A hosted 'broadcast mode' with clean overlays and one-click clip export, sold to newsrooms and streamers.
Custom branded globe installations for science museums and corporate lobbies.

steal_this: Wrap it as a stock-footage generator: let creators type a location and date, auto-record a cinematic 15-second flyover of the live scene, and sell the clips.
